AWS launches Graviton5 servers promising 40% better price performance

Published 2026-10-07 16:30 UTC

Amazon Web Services on Wednesday made its fifth-generation Graviton processor generally available, offering new EC2 instances that it says deliver up to 40% better price performance than Graviton4 for databases, web servers and machine learning inference.

Graviton5 is an Arm-based chip designed by Annapurna Labs, the Israeli chip startup Amazon acquired in 2015. Each processor has 192 cores and supports DDR5 memory and PCIe Gen 6. The new M9g, C9g and R9g instances are available today in several AWS regions, with more regions to follow next year.

Customers including Pinterest, Snowflake and Epic Games tested the chips in preview. AWS has said more than half of the new compute capacity it added over the past two years runs on Graviton, as cloud providers push their own silicon to reduce reliance on Intel and AMD.

Amazon says Graviton5 instances deliver up to 40% better price performance than the previous generation for common workloads such as web servers, databases and data analytics. The chips are built on a 3-nanometer process and include more cores per processor, larger caches and faster memory support.

The new instances are available first in a handful of regions, with broader rollout planned over the next few months. Amazon said several large customers, including a streaming service and a financial data company, tested the chips before launch and reported lower costs for the same amount of work.

Graviton is part of Amazon's strategy to design its own silicon rather than relying entirely on Intel and AMD. The company also designs chips for machine learning training and inference. Analysts say custom chips help Amazon control costs and differentiate its cloud offerings from Microsoft and Google, which are pursuing similar strategies.

Developers moving to Graviton need software compiled for the Arm architecture. Most popular programming languages, databases and container images now support Arm, and Amazon offers tools to help customers test their applications. The company said more than half of new compute capacity it added last year ran on Graviton processors, a share it expects to grow with the new generation.
